GRADUATION PROJECT
"Asir Leaf": telling coffee-plant diseases apart from phone photos           2025/2026
● Collected 6,400 leaf photos with two farmers' cooperatives in the Asir highlands and labelled them with an agronomist.
● Threw out blurred shots, and evened out the classes by rotating, flipping and cropping photos of the rarer diseases.
● Started from a network already trained on everyday images and retrained its last layers on our leaves, using PyTorch.
● Kept back every photo from one farm that the model never saw during training, and reported precision and recall per disease with a confusion matrix, not a single accuracy figure.
● Tried 24 combinations of learning rate, batch size and number of frozen layers and kept the one that scored best on the validation photos.
● Shrank the finished model until it answers in under a second on a mid-range Android phone with no internet, and wrapped it in a small app that eleven farmers used for a month.
● Result: 93% of test photos assigned to the right disease (five classes). Supervisor's grade: A+.

OTHER COURSEWORK
Used-car prices (Artificial Intelligence course, 2025)
● Predicted asking prices from 18,000 Saudi classified adverts, comparing linear regression, a random forest and gradient boosting; the boosted model was off by 9% on average.
